tools/tests-all/test_render.py::test_cou: List five tests. Only the first test passed in the older run.
Give four other tests different outcomes in the new run, leaving the first without a result.
The new summary must show one pass out of five listed tests, not two. Among the two tests with a pass or failure, the pass rate must be 50%.
tools/tests-all/test_render.py::test_pag: Give a test an unusual name containing an HTML tag. Put a script tag in its failure message.
Generate a report containing these strings and follow its links by matching their target IDs.
Every link must point to one place in the same page. The message must appear as text rather than executable HTML.
tools/tests-all/test_render.py::test_zer: Prepare one inventory with a blocked test and another with no recorded runs.
Render both reports without any pass or failure verdicts.
Neither report may imply a measured pass rate. The second must identify itself as an inventory only.
tools/tests-all/test_render.py::test_unk: Give the report a result whose status is ‘looks fine’, rather than one of the defined outcomes.
Ask the renderer to publish that result.
It must reject the unknown status rather than turn it into a verdict.
tools/tests-all/test_run.py::test_runner: Start with a previously passing report and one test in the current inventory.
Make the runner raise an error instead of returning a verdict.
Replace the old report with a blocked observation, include the reason, and return an unsuccessful exit status.
tools/tests-all/test_run.py::test_append: Give a fault scenario two names and a link to a separate log file.
Select it by its alternate name and embed the explanation in the repository report.
Keep the explanatory text. Do not copy conflicting section IDs or a link that would require another file.
tools/tests-all/test_inventory.py::test_: Collect the test inventory from this checkout.
Check the order, identity and required fields of each entry.
Every ID must be unique and sorted. Each entry must name its suite, setup, action, expectation and runner.
Read the SQLite workload definitions and the live device and seeded test lists.
Compare their report entries against the supported combinations.
List 29 workload/profile pairs for each filesystem, eight live I/O scenarios, and both the seed sweep and saved replay. Do not invent an unsupported journal mode.
Two Rust binaries share tests in a common source file. The library also contains a documentation example.
Find their test names as Cargo would see them.
Keep each binary’s separate execution identity, and match the documentation example by item and source line.
Create temporary Rust and Python source files containing new tests.
Discover their test names without executing them.
Both new tests must appear; discovery must not create Rust build output.
Put a Rust test function in a file that no crate target includes.
Try to inventory this source tree.
Stop with a discovery error instead of silently excluding the test.
tools/tests-all/test_execute.py::test_ch: The caller supplies a path intended only for a crash-test child and chooses a temporary directory.
Start a new test command through the repository runner and inspect the two settings it received.
Keep the caller’s temporary directory, but remove the crash-test path. A test must not accidentally overwrite the caller’s file.
tools/tests-all/test_execute.py::test_ou: Use child programs that exceed either a small output budget or a one-second time limit.
Run them through the report collector.
Stop the programs, retain only bounded output, and say which limit prevented completion.
tools/tests-all/test_execute.py::test_st: Make a Python suite that prints a fake failure, fails a real subtest and skips a test. List one additional missing test.
Keep the real pass, failure and skip separate; mark the missing case blocked rather than interpreting printed text as a verdict.
tools/tests-all/test_execute.py::test_ru: Prepare Rust test-program output containing a pass, failure, ignored test and documentation example.
Preserve all four outcomes, including the ignored test as not run.
tools/tests-all/test_execute.py::test_pa: Require three repetitions for a matrix case.
Supply records with all three passes, an explicit failure, or a missing repetition.
Only three passes can pass the case. A recorded failure must fail it; an incomplete set without a failure has no verdict.
tools/tests-all/test_execute.py::test_gu: Present a Linux host without explicit permission to use its devices.
Ask the runner to execute a guest-only scenario.
Mark it blocked without spawning any lab process.
